# A Beginner's Guide to Using ChatGPT Voice for Hands-Free Tasks

Imagine having a friendly assistant who can help you brainstorm dinner ideas while your hands are covered in flour, or keep you company with a custom story while you fold the washing. ChatGPT has a feature that lets you do exactly this—allowing you to have a natural, spoken conversation without looking at your screen. 

By the end of this guide, you will know how to start a hands-free voice conversation to help you organise your day-to-day life while multitasking.

## Before you start
- **The app:** Download the official ChatGPT app on your smartphone (available for both iPhone and Android). 
- **An account:** Make sure you are signed in to your free or paid OpenAI account.
- **A clear space:** Find a spot with a relatively quiet background so the microphone can pick up your voice easily.

## Step 1 — Find the headphones icon
To start speaking, you need to open the voice mode. This is called **real-time voice** (a feature that lets you speak to the AI and hear it speak back instantly, just like a normal phone call).

Open the ChatGPT app on your phone. Look at the bottom right-hand corner of the screen, right next to the text box where you would normally type. Tap the small icon that looks like a pair of headphones. 

## Step 2 — Choose a voice that you like
If this is your first time using the voice feature, the app will ask you to choose a voice. 

Speak into your phone to test the options. Swipe through the different voice choices, tap each one to hear how they sound, and select the one you find most pleasant. Tap the "Choose" or "Confirm" button to lock in your choice. You can easily change this later in your settings if you want to try a different tone.

## Step 3 — Give your first spoken prompt
Now, the screen will change to a simple, clean interface, indicating that the app is listening. You can now speak your first **prompt** (the instructions, questions, or topics you give to the AI). 

There is no need to press or hold any buttons while you speak. Just talk naturally, as if you are on a phone call with a friend.

💬 Example: Try saying: *"I have some leftover roast chicken, half a pumpkin, and some spinach in the fridge. What is a quick, warm dinner I can make with these?"*

## Step 4 — Listen and reply
Once you stop speaking, the app will pause for a second, process what you said, and speak its response back to you. 

You do not need to tap the screen to reply. When the AI finishes speaking, simply speak back. You can ask it to adjust its recipe, explain a step more slowly, or suggest a completely different idea.

💬 Example: If the suggestion sounds too complicated, you can say: *"That sounds nice, but I only have fifteen minutes. Can we make a simpler version of that?"*

## Step 5 — Go hands-free
Now that you know how the flow works, you can put your phone on the kitchen bench, slip it into your pocket with headphones on, or place it on the car console while you commute. 

You can ask the AI to help you learn something new, practice a conversational language, or even act as an interactive storyteller while you go about your chores.

💬 Example: While you are folding laundry, try saying: *"Tell me a short mystery story, but stop every two minutes so I can try to guess who the suspect is."*

To end the conversation at any time, simply tap the red cross icon or the "Stop" button on your screen.

## Common mistakes
- **Pausing too long mid-sentence:** If you stop to think for too long, the AI might assume you have finished speaking and start responding. If this happens, simply say, *"Wait, I wasn't finished yet,"* and continue your thought.
- **Background noise interference:** Loud noises like a running tap, sizzling frying pan, or loud traffic can confuse the microphone. If you are in a noisy room, using wireless earbuds with a built-in microphone will make a massive difference.
- **Speaking like a computer search:** You do not need to use rigid keywords like *"Recipe pumpkin chicken fast."* Talk to the AI using normal, casual sentences. It is designed to understand everyday human speech.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** You can reclaim "lost" time. Mundane chores like washing the dishes, vacuuming, or weeding the garden can become opportunities to brainstorm a weekend plan, learn about a historical event, or prep a shopping list.
- **For your business or work:** You can use your commute to dictate drafts of emails, practice public speaking, or talk through a difficult problem out loud to get a fresh perspective.
- **If you're just getting started:** The easiest first step is to use it in the kitchen. It keeps your phone screen clean of sticky fingers and makes cooking a much more interactive experience.
